primitives.name: Private Property Incentive Function
primitives.verbatim_quote: The social justification of private ownership is that the coupling of control of resources with enjoyment of the fruits of their use is supposed to give an incentive to use the goods effectively in production.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'I': 'incentive strength (dimensionless)', 'C': 'control over resources (units of control)', 'F': 'fruit of use (units of benefit)'}
primitives.assumptions: Incentive function is monotonic in control and fruit; diminishing marginal returns assumed.

layer2.mapping: Incentive function maps to GSI's Bayesian utility maximization under uncertainty, where I represents expected utility gain from resource control.
layer2.telemetry: Observed productivity gains in controlled vs. communal resource usage

primitives.name: Unprogressive Society Property Regime
primitives.verbatim_quote: The same reasoning applies to property in material things, but in an unprogressive state the force of the argument is relatively weak.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'S': 'societal progress level (dimensionless)', 'R': 'regime strength of property incentive (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: R is a decreasing function of S; S = 0 implies no effective property incentive.

layer2.mapping: Represents GSE's transition kernel from routine production to dynamic innovation, where low S leads to static resource regimes.
layer2.telemetry: Historical shifts in societal structure and corresponding changes in property enforcement

primitives.name: Slavery vs Freedom Efficiency Tradeoff
primitives.verbatim_quote: An adequate discussion of the inotives involved in the production of such surplus wealth would be beyond the scope of this work.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'E_f': 'efficiency of free labor (dimensionless)', 'E_s': 'efficiency of slave labor (dimensionless)', 'C_f': 'cost of freedom (currency units)', 'C_s': 'cost of slavery (currency units)'}
primitives.assumptions: E_f > E_s and C_f < C_s in equilibrium.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When E_f - E_s < 0 or C_s - C_f < 0, system favors slavery.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's cost-benefit analysis of labor incentives, where freedom is modeled as a higher-value control mechanism.
layer2.telemetry: Labor productivity metrics across different institutional frameworks

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that private property functions as an incentive mechanism linking resource control to productive outcomes. This is formalized through a utility-based model where the incentive I depends on the product of control C and benefit F. In progressive societies, this relationship is strong due to innovation and dynamic production. In unprogressive ones, the regime strength R diminishes, leading to static or inefficient resource allocation. The efficiency tradeoff between slavery and freedom shows that freedom is economically superior when productivity gains outweigh enforcement costs. These primitives form a dual structure: one of incentive alignment and another of institutional efficiency, both grounded in economic rationality and bounded by historical context.
